cohort: Two hundred children aged from birth to two years old were randomly selected from Maternity and Pediatrics Teaching Hospitals in Sulaymaniyah city.
finding: Oral mucosal lesions were observed in 64.5% of children, with Epstein pearls and Bohn's nodule being the most frequent diagnoses, and lesions were more common in children within their first week of life.
mod_finding: The study found that 64% of the children were delivered by cesarean section and significant differences were present between breastfeeding and mode of delivery.
cross-section timing: Children aged from birth to two years old were observed at a single point in time.
